recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group still wants a distinct canonical StructureDefinition/Type instead of the current Base/DataType framework, raise and apply that as a new model-change issue rather than as a FHIR-23842 reconciliation fix.
issue_request: FHIR-23842 was a Published/Persuasive MnM change request asking to formally define the abstract type "Type" because it existed in reference implementations and UML definitions but did not exist formally; the approved resolution was to define it formally in R5.
initial_application: No FHIR-23842-keyed implementation commit was found. The relevant application appears to be the unkeyed commit cbdf7d1e55dc4bfa1dc30fc526edee0491e05782, "rebuild abstract type framework," which introduced formal Base/DataType/PrimitiveType/BackboneType source spreadsheets and fhir.ini wiring.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists the abstract infrastructure types and page mappings, and source/types.html defines the FHIR Type Framework as the base abstract types that provide the foundation for datatypes, resources, and logical models. R5 and current build publication checks expose abstract Base and DataType StructureDefinitions and no type.profile.json. Later FHIR-53296 is only Resolved - change required in this default run and concerns abstract grouping metadata for existing Base/DataType, not adding a separate Type artifact.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding a new canonical Type now would be a substantive model change and would conflict with the already-published Base/DataType framework used by R5 and the current build.

related_jiras.note: Later Resolved - change required issue asks to move Base and DataType into an abstract display group, confirming the existing abstract types but not establishing a final Applied/Published decision to add StructureDefinition/Type.
